finding.title: Make E2E-1108 in infra_p1_test.dart exercise the real ReminderEnabled notifier instead of round-tripping SharedPreferences
finding.rule: TQ-8 (tautological / weaker than the failure modes of the code under test)

evidence.quote: group('E2E-1108 — Per-profile notification prefs isolated on profile switch', () {
await prefs.setBool(keyB, false);
final aValue = prefs.getBool(keyA) ?? true;

finding.why: The test titled 'Per-profile notification prefs isolated on profile switch' never switches the active profile and never instantiates the real ReminderEnabled Riverpod notifier — it calls prefs.setBool(keyB, false) and then asserts prefs.getBool(keyB) is false, which only proves the SharedPreferences mock stores what it was told (an SDK behavior, not app logic). reminderEnabledKey() is a one-line string formatter (base + profileId). A real regression this journey is meant to catch — e.g. ReminderEnabled.build() caching profile A's value after activeProfileIdProvider flips to B, or the notifier writing under the wrong profile's key — would not be caught here because the notifier is never built or read through ref. The in-file comment even concedes 'provider rebuilds on activeProfileIdProvider are covered by the widget itself' without pointing to where.
finding.recommendation: Drive the real flow: mount /notifications for profile A, toggle the reminder switch, then swap the active identity (second E2EHarness or an activeProfileIdProvider override simulating profile B) and assert the widget/notifier reflects B's independently-loaded state, not just that two SharedPreferences keys hold different bytes.
acceptance_criteria: E2E-1108 fails red if ReminderEnabled.build() is changed to ignore activeProfileIdProvider and read a single shared key.
Test reads the reminder toggle state through the widget tree (not direct SharedPreferences access) for at least one of the two profiles.

finding.title: Split 8 of 9 t1-test-cross-p2 e2e journey files under the AG-3 400-line cap
finding.why: AG-3's stated enforcement checker ('find lib test -name *.dart ... | xargs wc -l | awk $1>400') explicitly sweeps test/ as well as lib/, and the digest names a 401-line file as its own canonical P3 example. 8 of the 9 files in this batch exceed the cap, two by more than double (982, 924 lines) — consistent with AG-3's stated rationale that oversized files exceed per-file agent read budgets and become dumping grounds, which this batch's own duplication finding (fakes hand-rolled per file instead of shared) illustrates.
finding.recommendation: Split each file along its existing '── E2E-nnn ──' group boundaries into one file per journey-cluster, and extract the shared fakes/override-builders (see the duplication finding) into a common module to shrink each file's boilerplate share.
acceptance_criteria: find learning_tracker/test -name '*.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400 {print}' lists none of the 8 files (or a documented, reviewed exception).
AG-3 checker script lands per Rule 0 and runs in make audit / CI.
